title: Identification of Patterns of Morphological Organization of Visual Organs at the Development of Malignant Neoplasms in Cats
content: Paraneoplastic syndromes are clinical and laboratory manifestations of the tumor process. The aim of the work: to study the “morphological-functional indices” (MFIs) of organs and systems in animals in terms of the development of malignant neoplasms based on the “histological-pathological” analysis of the eyeballs after bilateral and unilateral enucleating. The study of MFIs of visual organs and systems in animals in terms of the development of malignant neoplasms was performed based on the “histological-pathological” analysis of the eyeballs after bilateral and unilateral enucleating in a total of 19 cats, admitted to a veterinary clinics in Moscow for diagnostic and therapeutic manipulations. Results: Histological changes were detected in about 37% of the cats in the studied sample with significant changes - only in the iris (cornea) of the cats in the experimental (control) group. The most sensitive of the eyeball structures in the study was the iris. In about 21% of cases, “histological-pathological” examinations established or clarified the oncological diagnosis: melanoma, lymphoma. In about 17% of cats in the experimental group, ophthalmological syndrome in the form of iris cysts, which developed against the background of oncological diseases, was histologically confirmed. Conclusions: The study of MFIs of the visual organ in terms of the development of malignant neoplasms in animals is important, since it allows not only to confirm the presence of a tumor, but also to clarify its variant and individual characteristics, which determines the treatment regimen.
